questions.q: Given const wallets = ["a", "b", "c"], what does wallets[0] return?
questions.explain: The first element of an array is always at index 0 in JavaScript.

questions.q: What is the difference between transaction.from and transaction["from"]?
options: Dot notation is faster at runtime than bracket notation in every case
Nothing functionally — dot and bracket notation access the same property; brackets are required when the property name is stored in a variable
transaction["from"] only works on arrays, not objects
questions.explain: Both access the same property; bracket notation is necessary for dynamic or non-identifier property names.

questions.q: Given const obj = { a: 1 }, what does obj.b evaluate to?
options: undefined — accessing a missing property doesn't throw an error
questions.explain: JavaScript object property access is forgiving — a missing property simply evaluates to undefined.

questions.q: In block.transactions[0].to, what is being chained together?
options: Property access (block.transactions, then .to) and array indexing ([0])
Two unrelated variables with no connection
questions.explain: This reads the transactions array property off block, indexes its first element, then reads that element's to property.

questions.q: What does .push() do to an array?
options: Removes the first element of the array
Returns the array's length without modifying it
Adds a new element to the end of the array
questions.explain: push() appends one or more elements to the end of an array, increasing its length.
